markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **terminal allocation with preserved branch-specific contexts and persistent accounting**. At 30% progress, resolving the existing attribution gap offers a stronger foundation than adding adaptive optimization.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, terminal-example probability and objective weight differ: separately normalized active branches each contribute coefficient mass 0.5. Increasing terminal allocation therefore changes sampling and target volume without necessarily increasing its coefficient share. Second, all training-allocation snapshots are null and sampler bookkeeping is unmatched. Diagnostic terminal coverage cannot verify whether p=0.75 was implemented. Third, Electronics and Industrial have weaker sampled separation and more concentrated user representations. These associations identify diagnostic priorities but establish neither causality nor validation performance.

Three literature insights guide the design. BERT4Rec [1] includes terminal masking to align training with appended-MASK inference. This supports the intervention, without establishing 0.75 as optimal. PCGrad [2] distinguishes conflicting gradient directions from objective allocation. Conflict probes can inform later experiments without changing this trial. GradNorm [3] addresses gradient magnitude imbalance. Equal coefficient mass therefore does not imply equal optimization influence.

The framework separates three research directions:

| Direction | Intervention or probe | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision allocation | Context-preserving p=0.75 | Target-volume and sampling effects |
| Optimization interaction | Frozen-batch gradient measurements | Local measurements may not generalize |
| Behavioral dependence | Matched recent/older deletion | Sensitivity does not establish usefulness |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration; difficulty scores increase with implementation burden:

1. **Context-preserving allocation with persisted provenance** [1]. Originality **3/10**: improves attribution; terminal masking is established. Potential **7/10**: supports reproducible follow-up; effects remain benchmark-specific. Difficulty **3/10**: small sampler change; branch-context fidelity needs care.
2. **Read-only branch-gradient audit** [2,3]. Originality **4/10**: connects allocation to optimization; gradient diagnostics are established. Potential **6/10**: identifies candidate interference; local conflicts need not predict HR@10. Difficulty **5/10**: uses autograd; preserving stochastic state requires care.
3. **Matched recent-versus-older deletion probe**. Originality **4/10**: targets stale-interest feedback; perturbation methods are familiar. Potential **6/10**: reveals context dependence; deletion changes information availability. Difficulty **4/10**: requires no additional model; controls require careful construction.

Select idea 1. Preserve each baseline branch’s own context generator, corruption rules, reduction, and empty-branch policy; never replace sampled-prefix terminal contexts with latest-history windows. Persist exact counts and loss accounting alongside the checkpoint so diagnostics survive reload. Train one BERT4Rec per category and select solely through unchanged macro validation HR@10. No validation improvement is supplied or claimed.

References: [1] [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690); [2] [PCGrad](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782); [3] [GradNorm](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.02257).

idea.description: Prespecify terminal-only example allocation p=0.75 while preserving the corrected BERT4Rec baseline’s branch-specific context generators, random corruption, loss reduction, and branch-presence policy. Persist measured allocation and objective accounting with each category checkpoint.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnosis cannot verify actual training allocation: all runtime snapshots are null and diagnostic batches lack matched sampler bookkeeping. Furthermore, the supplied history identifies a context-construction confound. A context-preserving allocation experiment addresses these gaps before introducing gradient adaptation or representation regularization. It does not directly resolve unobserved ownership, compatibility, or current intent.
idea.implementation_notes:
The supplied baseline source is absent from this prompt, so implementation must use its actual generators rather than invent replacement training code. Record whether its allocation is paired or stochastic, the number of examples per optimizer step, branch-specific context distributions, original probability if defined, reduction, eligibility rules, and checkpoint selection. If converting paired allocation to stochastic allocation is necessary, disclose that protocol change explicitly; do not describe it as changing an existing probability alone. If p already equals 0.75, label the condition replication.

Preserve each branch's own generator. In particular, terminal contexts must retain the supplied sampled-prefix cutoff policy when present; random reconstruction must retain its own baseline windows, mask probability, replacements, and fallback. Conditional context distributions must remain unchanged. Keep terminal targets only in labels at their supervised position; do not introduce shifted-target leakage into bidirectional inputs.

Under the supplied separately normalized objective, each nonempty branch contributes 0.5 times its target-mean loss; empty branches contribute zero without redistribution. Preserve this exactly. For branch b with n_b valid targets, record detached CE sum S_b, n_b, per-target coefficient 0.5/n_b when active, coefficient mass 0.5, and objective contribution 0.5*S_b/n_b. Terminal coefficient share is 0.5 when both branches are active, 1 when only terminal is active, and 0 when only reconstruction is active; it is unavailable when neither is active. These coefficients are neither loss-value nor gradient shares. Persist per-epoch and cumulative counts, branch presence, terminal-position coverage, and mean batch objectives separately from global target-weighted CE.

Write accounting as checkpoint metadata or a trial-local sidecar keyed by category, checkpoint identity, and epoch. Report selected-checkpoint-epoch accounting separately from final-epoch accounting. Runtime counters must not disappear silently after state_dict reload. Diagnostic branch membership requires bookkeeping tied to the exact sequence, positive, and negative arrays; unmatched batches remain unavailable.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Preserve actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch compatibility, metadata references, and B x L loader tensors. Use only observed histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions.

Train exactly one independent BERT4Rec per category across Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and baseline optimizer, architecture, batch size, and checkpoint rule. Charge all training and diagnostics to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not access other trials or checkpoints.

At inference, retain at most L-1 history items, append reserved MASK, left-pad, and read the maximum nonpadding index. Preserve checkpoint/configuration/predictor-writer consistency; each route loads exactly one trained checkpoint. Use unchanged host validation macro HR@10 for selection. Geometry and training margins remain exploratory; no improvement or causal explanation is established by the supplied evidence.
idea.pseudocode:
P_TERMINAL = 0.75
spec = supplied_corrected_baseline_specification()
record_actual_allocation_context_and_reduction_protocol(spec)
# Paired-to-stochastic conversion, if required, must be explicitly disclosed.

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    model, optimizer = initialize_unchanged_baseline(category)
    for epoch in unchanged_training_schedule(max_epochs=200):
        accounting = new_epoch_accounting()
        for step in range(200):
            branches = baseline_seeded_allocation(P_TERMINAL)
            batch = []
            for branch in branches:
                # Preserve the generator conditional on branch.
                clean = baseline_context_generator[branch]()
                tokens, labels, provenance = baseline_corruptor[branch](clean)
                batch.append(baseline_left_pad(tokens, labels, provenance))
            features = model.log2feats(batch.tokens)
            loss = features.sum() * 0.0
            for branch in [TERMINAL, RECONSTRUCTION]:
                S, n = exact_baseline_branch_loss_sum_and_denominator(features, batch, branch)
                if n > 0:
                    contribution = 0.5 * S / n
                    loss = loss + contribution
                else:
                    contribution = loss.detach() * 0.0
                accounting.record_exact_detached_values(branch, S, n, contribution)
            accounting.record_branch_presence_and_exact_batch_provenance(batch)
            baseline_optimizer_step(optimizer, loss)
        persist_trial_local_epoch_accounting(category, epoch, accounting)
        apply_unchanged_checkpoint_selection()
    retain_one_checkpoint_with_matching_accounting_and_configuration(category)
write_matching_embedded_predictor()

# Predictor, routed by category:

# scores = model.predict_score(model.log2feats(tokens)[j], real_candidates)
# Host evaluates unchanged pinned validation candidates and macro HR@10.

originality.positive: Branch-specific context preservation and checkpoint-persistent accounting improve experimental attribution.
originality.negative: Terminal masking and allocation tuning are established techniques; this is an incremental protocol refinement.

future_potential.positive: An auditable allocation experiment provides a sound basis for later studies of gradient interaction and supervision efficiency.
future_potential.negative: Allocation still changes target volume and stochastic estimation, and one fixed-seed benchmark cannot establish broad transfer.

code_difficulty.positive: The backbone and predictor remain unchanged; the main changes concern allocation and accounting.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful implementation requires resolving paired versus stochastic allocation and preserving exact branch contexts and reduction semantics.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Includes last-item masking and appended-MASK prediction, motivating terminal supervision.
limitations: Does not establish p=0.75 as optimal for this benchmark.
Does not establish how the supplied baseline's branch allocation and reduction affect optimization.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Examines conflicting task-gradient directions and proposes projection-based gradient modification.
Motivates measuring terminal and reconstruction gradient interactions separately from coefficient mass.
limitations: Does not demonstrate improvements for this BERT4Rec task.
Local gradient conflict alone does not establish worse validation ranking.

related_work.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
contributions: Adapts task weights using gradient magnitudes and relative training rates.
Highlights that equal objective coefficients need not produce equal gradient influence.
limitations: Adaptive weighting would introduce an additional intervention beyond the selected allocation experiment.
Its results do not establish an appropriate balance for terminal and reconstruction objectives here.
